title: Text and Image Views knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the most direct learning goal for this lesson?
options: The main goal is to apply displaying text in a small Swift example and verify the result.
Use text and image views only for visual styling.
Skip type checking and accept any result.
Replace a focused example with unrelated code.
questions.answer_key: The main goal is to apply displaying text in a small Swift example and verify the result.
questions.explanation: Text and Image Views is best learned through a small, verifiable example. For displaying text, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

questions.prompt: Which practice supports maintainable Swift code?

Ignore ownership and errors when an example works once.
Use the newest API without checking target compatibility.
Use documented Swift semantics, explicit data flow and a test for a meaningful edge case.
questions.answer_key: Use documented Swift semantics, explicit data flow and a test for a meaningful edge case.
